agent-window.description: IPC for the detached AI chat window (label `agent`). It runs our own frontend bundle, so it gets the same core IPC as the main webview; browser-* windows (remote content) still match no capability at all.

clipbar.description: The clip toolbar window (clipbar-N, our own bundle, paired with browser-N). Using a prefix wildcard for webviews is an explicit exception to the "a capability does not use wildcards" principle: the label is minted by Rust alone (clipbar.rs), and a window holding remote content is always browser-* or reader and never matches this prefix. Tauri's ACL does not constrain an application's own custom commands one by one, so the allowlist below is a discipline list rather than an enforced boundary — what the toolbar actually calls is: clipbar_to_main / clipbar_set_expanded / browser_set_docked / browser_navigate / browser_back / browser_forward / browser_focus / browser_state / bookmark_toggle / bookmark_list / vault_current / vault_last / notes_list / query_blocks / note_create / clips_lookup / settings_get.

default.description: Default capability for the main window's own webview. Scoped to webviews (not windows) so any future webview attached to the main window does NOT inherit IPC — and browser-* windows never match at all.
